2. The facts relevant for disposal of the Rule as found in the averments of the writ petition, are that the respondent no.3 International Finance Investment and Commerce Bank Limited ("IFIC Bank"), Motijheel Branch, Dhaka as plaintiff filed Artha Rin Suit No.24 of 2006 before the Artha Rin Adalat No.3 Dhaka ("the Adalat") on 13.03.2005) for recovery of a sum of Tk.33,66,765.25 (as stood on 31.03.2005) impleading the petitioner and others as defendants. In the plaint, the status of the petitioner had been shown as 'daughter' of the then Managing Director, A.M. Aga Yusuf who was a guarantor of the loan availed by the defendant no.1-company. The said suit was decreed on 03.06.2010 on contest against the defendant nos. 1, 3-6, 10 & 11 and ex-partee against the defendant no.12 (petitioner herein). The decree holder Bank put the decree into execution in Execution Case No.140 of 2010. At one stage of the execution proceeding, the petitioner who had been impleaded as defendant no.12 in the suit, filed an application on 31.10.2013 under Order 1, rule 10(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure read with section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as "the Ain") for striking out her name from the execution proceedings. After hearing the parties and on consideration of the materials on record, the Adalat vide impugned order dated 30.01.2014 rejected the said prayer of the petitioner holding, inter alia, that the executing court had no authority to strike out the name of or to implead any person in the proceeding. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order of the Adalat, the petitioner approached this Court and obtained the Rule as stated above. 

 7. It appears that one A.M. Aga Yusuf former Managing Director of the respondent no. 4-company executed a letter of guarantee in favour of the respondent no. 3 —Bank to secure the credit facilities availed by the company. After his death, the Bank impleaded his daughter Dr. Momtaz Yusuf as defendant no. 12 in the Artha Rin Suit. The suit was decreed on contest against some of the defendants but ex-parte against petitioner, which the execution case pursuant to the decree was being proceeded with, the petitioner's application for striking out her name from the execution proceeding was rejected by the impugned order. 

 12. Having regard to the above we hold that the decree holder bank can execute the decree in accordance with law against the judgment debtor (s) who are lawfully liable to repay the decreetal amount along with the interest if any.
